# SPE Round 3 Plan

## Core point

Round 3 fixes the C tool split (F4). It adds a separate hard slice of tickets and raises trials to 5. It retires config D. Round 2 over-predicted every miss. All four misses landed below the prediction, and the naive baseline was closer in 4 of 5 rows. So round 3 predictions stay close to the baseline. Each predicted move ties to a failure ID.

I will commit locally after each SPE step. I will not push. Commit messages will carry no attribution lines.

## Gaps I found in the round 2 record

1. **The priority baseline from round 1 is suspect.** F5 regraded round 2 only. Round 1 priority (0.78) likely came from the old grader, which read the draft reply. So the round 2 verdict "naive closer" on C priority compares a fixed grader to a buggy one. I will regrade round 1 priority with the fixed grade.py and add a note to that row. I will not rewrite the round 2 verdict.
2. **P2 would break the baseline if the new tickets are merged in.** The "same as last round" numbers only apply to the round 2 ticket set. I will keep the 10 hard tickets as a separate slice. Every metric gets reported per slice.
3. **n=5 does not remove all noise.** Five trials cut trial-to-trial noise. They do not cut ticket sampling noise. I will report a 95% interval per cell that covers both. Then the claim "B's miss is inside noise" becomes something round 3 can test.
4. **Claude would write the hard ticket labels.** That is a contamination risk. I will write the tickets and labels before any config sees them. I will flag them for your review. The hard slice gets reported apart so it cannot move the frozen comparisons.
5. **The draft baseline lists D at 0.74.** D is retired, so I will remove that line.

## Step 2. Prediction (commit 2)

Rename `spe/predictions/r03-draft.yaml` to `spe/predictions/r03.yaml`. Set `status: locked`. Remove D from the baseline. The prediction is locked before any round 3 run starts. The commit hash goes into the eval run record.

### Scored predictions (frozen slice, n=5)

| Metric | Config | Predicted | Same as last round | Why |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| category accuracy | A | 0.86 | 0.86 | A did not change. |
| category accuracy | B | 0.86 | 0.86 | B did not change. In round 2, B's addition did not beat A. |
| category accuracy | C | 0.82 | 0.80 | The split brings back the status check. That helps outage tickets. The merge also folded other tools, and those stay merged. So only part of the 0.04 drop should come back. |
| priority accuracy | C | 0.76 | 0.71 | F4 sent outage tickets to P3 because C never called the status check. With the check exposed, C should call it on most outage tickets. |

**Pre-lock sizing rule for C priority.** Before I lock, I will count the round 2 C trials where F4 caused a priority miss. Call that share k. Then the prediction is 0.71 + 0.7 × k, rounded to two places. If the result differs from 0.76, the yaml uses the computed number, and the yaml notes why.

### Mechanism predictions (pass or fail)

These rows have no round 2 baseline that meets the hit rule. A and B priority accuracy will be recorded. All hard slice numbers for A, B, and C will be recorded. They become round 4 baselines.

## Step 4. Dynamic workflow (commit 4)

Write the workflow script to `spe/evals/r03/workflow`. Write a short run plan to `spe/plans/r03-plan.md`. The script reads configs, slices, and the trial count from the spec at runtime. Nothing is hard-coded. Every subagent the workflow spawns uses Opus. The configs under test keep their own models.

| Stage | What it does | Gate |
|---|---|---|
| 0. Preflight | Checks that the prediction file is locked and committed and records its hash. Checks the frozen slice hash against round 2. Checks that C exposes the status tool. Checks that D is absent. Runs the grader guard test. Checks that the hard slice has 10 labeled tickets. | Any failed check stops the run. |
| 1. Run | Fans out configs (A, B, C) × slices (frozen, hard) × 5 trials. Saves each transcript to `runs/<config>/<slice>/<ticket>/<trial>`. Infra errors get up to 2 harness retries. Each retry is logged apart from agent behavior. | The trial count is fixed. Nothing gets added after results appear. |
| 2. Grade | grade.py scores every transcript. Then one Opus agent per config checks 10 random graded items against the labels. | Any grader disagreement stops scoring and opens an F entry. |
| 3. Score | A script computes each metric per cell and slice with a 95% interval. It writes the round 3 section of `spe/prediction-log.md` with the Verdict and Closer columns. It also scores M1 to M4. | Numbers come from the script, not from a model. |
| 4. Triage | Spawns one Opus agent per miss and per failed mechanism check. Each agent reads the failing transcripts and names which Why broke, with transcript IDs. The agents write new F entries to `spe/failures.md` and update F4. | The number of agents depends on the number of misses. |
| 5. Propose | Appends "Proposed for round 4 (not yet agreed)" to the spec. Each proposal cites an F entry or a scored row. | Nothing gets agreed automatically. |
